main_body: Tall rounded-top standing stone slab, dark grey, with three cyan rune glyphs on its south face
top_band: light grey band at rows ~7-10 with rounded back corners, about 3-4 rows, spanning the full width; a dark line at ~row 10-11 separates it from the front face
evidence: The column read from row 6 downward gives a short light-grey cap of 3-4 rows, a dark line, then one long flat dark face to row ~30. The cap is a flat band like the red 'column: flat band cap' guide, not an ellipse or cut face that reads as a horizontal surface. There is no distinct lighter front-edge line and no eave shadow. The runes are painted flat on the face and not inset. It reads as a front elevation with a hat, so it fails.

style.evidence: The stone body has about 3 greys (light cap, dark face, slightly lighter left strip) inside a thick near-black outline that goes all the way round, the sticker look. Large areas of the face are a single flat dark tone with no grain, chips or speckle. The only detail is the cyan runes. Per-tile colour counts are far below the stall and well references, which carry tile scallops, wood grain and stone-by-stone shading.
